name: KinStudy Offline Study Database
description: Verified foundational Mathematics and Science formulas and concepts for instant offline lookup.

entries.title: Quadratic Formula
entries.question: What is the quadratic formula?
entries.answer: For an equation ax² + bx + c = 0, where a ≠ 0, the solutions are x = (-b ± √(b² - 4ac)) / (2a). The expression b² - 4ac is called the discriminant.

entries.title: Pythagorean Theorem
entries.question: What is the Pythagorean theorem?
entries.answer: For a right-angled triangle, a² + b² = c², where a and b are the two perpendicular sides and c is the hypotenuse.

entries.title: Area of a Circle
entries.question: What is the area of a circle?
entries.answer: The area of a circle is A = πr², where r is the radius.

entries.title: Circumference of a Circle
entries.question: What is the circumference of a circle?
entries.answer: The circumference of a circle is C = 2πr, where r is the radius. It can also be written as C = πd, where d is the diameter.

entries.title: Area of a Rectangle
entries.question: What is the area of a rectangle?
entries.answer: The area of a rectangle is A = length × width.

entries.title: Area of a Triangle
entries.question: What is the area of a triangle?
entries.answer: The area of a triangle is A = ½ × base × height.

entries.title: Percentage
entries.question: How do you calculate a percentage?
entries.answer: Percentage = (part ÷ whole) × 100.

entries.title: Simple Interest
entries.question: What is the simple interest formula?
entries.answer: Simple Interest = (P × R × T) / 100, where P is principal, R is annual rate of interest in percent, and T is time in years.

entries.title: Speed, Distance and Time
entries.question: What are the speed distance time formulas?
entries.answer: Speed = Distance ÷ Time. Distance = Speed × Time. Time = Distance ÷ Speed.

entries.title: Arithmetic Mean
entries.question: How do you calculate the average?
entries.answer: Arithmetic mean = Sum of all values ÷ Number of values.

entries.title: Laws of Exponents
entries.question: What are common laws of exponents?
entries.answer: For suitable nonzero bases: aᵐ × aⁿ = aᵐ⁺ⁿ; aᵐ ÷ aⁿ = aᵐ⁻ⁿ; (aᵐ)ⁿ = aᵐⁿ; a⁰ = 1.

entries.title: Distance Between Two Points
entries.question: What is the distance formula between two points?
entries.answer: For points (x₁, y₁) and (x₂, y₂), distance = √[(x₂ - x₁)² + (y₂ - y₁)²].

entries.title: Newton's Second Law
entries.question: What is Newton's second law?
entries.answer: Newton's second law is commonly written as F = ma, where F is net force, m is mass, and a is acceleration.

entries.title: Weight
entries.question: What is the formula for weight?
entries.answer: Weight is the gravitational force acting on an object. Near Earth's surface, W = mg, where m is mass and g is gravitational acceleration.

entries.title: Density
entries.question: What is the density formula?
entries.answer: Density = Mass ÷ Volume. In symbols, ρ = m/V.

entries.title: Mechanical Work
entries.question: What is the formula for work?
entries.answer: When a constant force acts in the direction of displacement, work = force × displacement. More generally, W = Fd cosθ, where θ is the angle between force and displacement.

entries.title: Power
entries.question: What is the formula for power?
entries.answer: Average power = Work ÷ Time. It is also the rate at which energy is transferred or work is done.

entries.title: Kinetic Energy
entries.question: What is kinetic energy?
entries.answer: The kinetic energy of an object of mass m moving at speed v is KE = ½mv².

entries.title: Gravitational Potential Energy
entries.question: What is gravitational potential energy near Earth's surface?
entries.answer: Near Earth's surface, gravitational potential energy relative to a chosen reference level is approximately PE = mgh, where m is mass, g is gravitational acceleration, and h is height above the reference level.

entries.title: Ohm's Law
entries.question: What is Ohm's law?
entries.answer: For an ohmic conductor under appropriate constant physical conditions, V = IR, where V is potential difference, I is current, and R is resistance.

entries.title: Electrical Power
entries.question: What is electrical power?
entries.answer: Electrical power can be calculated as P = VI. Using Ohm's law, equivalent forms include P = I²R and P = V²/R when the relationships apply.

entries.title: Wave Speed
entries.question: What is the wave speed formula?
entries.answer: Wave speed is v = fλ, where v is wave speed, f is frequency, and λ is wavelength.

entries.title: Newton's First Law
entries.question: What is Newton's first law?
entries.answer: An object remains at rest or continues moving with constant velocity in a straight line unless acted upon by a net external force.

entries.title: Newton's Third Law
entries.question: What is Newton's third law?
entries.answer: When two objects interact, they exert forces on each other that are equal in magnitude and opposite in direction.

entries.title: Conservation of Energy
entries.question: What is the law of conservation of energy?
entries.answer: Energy cannot be created or destroyed in an isolated system; it can be transferred between objects or transformed from one form to another.

entries.title: Photosynthesis
entries.question: What is photosynthesis?
entries.answer: Photosynthesis is the process by which photosynthetic organisms use light energy to convert carbon dioxide and water into energy-rich organic compounds such as glucose, releasing oxygen in oxygenic photosynthesis. A simplified overall equation is 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂, with light energy involved.

entries.title: Aerobic Cellular Respiration
entries.question: What is aerobic cellular respiration?
entries.answer: Aerobic cellular respiration is a set of metabolic reactions in which cells extract energy from organic molecules such as glucose, using oxygen as the final electron acceptor in the main aerobic pathway and producing ATP, carbon dioxide, and water.

entries.title: Basic Structure of an Atom
entries.question: What are the main particles in an atom?
entries.answer: An atom contains a nucleus made primarily of protons and neutrons, with electrons occupying regions around the nucleus. Protons have positive electric charge, electrons have negative electric charge, and neutrons have no net electric charge.

entries.title: pH Scale
entries.question: What does the pH scale measure?
entries.answer: pH is a measure related to the activity or concentration of hydrogen ions in an aqueous solution. At 25°C, a pH below 7 is acidic, pH 7 is neutral for pure water under standard conditions, and pH above 7 is basic.

entries.title: Conservation of Mass
entries.question: What is conservation of mass in a chemical reaction?
entries.answer: In a closed system undergoing an ordinary chemical reaction, the total mass of the reactants equals the total mass of the products.
